findings.text: Statmount query entry validates flags, copies variable request, resolves target by open file or by namespace, denies foreign namespace without privilege, allocates kernel state, runs guarded fill, copies result to user, retries with larger scratch on transient overflow, and releases scratch and root each attempt.

Listmount entry validates flags, caps requested count, checks user range, copies request, prepares cursor plus id buffer plus namespace reference, rejects foreign namespace access without privilege, enumerates under shared protection, copies collected ids back, and returns count or error.

By file descriptor the query uses the file path mount and derives its namespace, clearing point and namespace id requests when detached so no namespace exists; by id it rejects empty namespace when an id filter is given and missing mount; it then obtains a reference root and enforces reachability or admin capability except for file mode before a security statfs check.

After caching the idmap pointer once, the query fills basic mount, basic superblock and propagation source when requested, then each requested string field in a fixed order stopping at first failure, then namespace id and supported mask; it warns if any returned mask bit lies outside the supported set.

String field helper ensures a leading empty byte exists, records start offset, dispatches by flag to type, root, point, options, option arrays, subtype, source and idmap renderers, warns and fails on unknown flag, leaves mask unset when nothing was emitted, checks header plus payload size against user length and scratch overflow, then terminates with zero and records mask and offset.

Combined mount options emit security options first then filesystem hook output when present, request retry on overflow, leave caller unchanged when empty, otherwise remove the leading separator by shifting the remainder down one byte.

Filesystem only and security only array variants each capture their respective hook output then transform it into counted zero separated entries and store the count in the matching numeric field, propagating retry or overflow signals.

Option list transform checks overflow, skips the initial separator, truncates to empty when no payload exists, otherwise splits on commas, decodes octal escapes in place, counts entries, and fails if the count would reach maximum integer.

Filesystem type always reports the type name, subtype reports only when present, and source prefers the filesystem devname hook with unescaping and overflow detection, falling back to the stored device name when that hook is absent.

User and group idmap helpers each render mappings for their direction, store entry count, and raise the matching mask bit whenever the mount has a valid idmap even when zero entries were valid for the caller, distinguishing non idmapped mounts from fully filtered idmapped mounts.

Result copy places payload bytes after the fixed header in the user buffer, copies the smaller of user length and header size for the header, sets total size to header portion plus payload length, and reports fault if either user copy fails.

List enumeration resolves a reference root, treats a special root parent as that root else looks up the parent mount, enforces reachability or admin plus a security check, selects a start cursor from first or last or neighbour after or before the last id according to direction, then walks tree order collecting reachable descendants up to capacity while skipping the parent itself.

Requested root helper for own namespace duplicates current process root; for a foreign namespace it fails when empty, otherwise selects the first non root child of the namespace root as representative and references its mount and dentry, failing when no such child exists.

Namespace resolution prefers explicit namespace id lookup, else validates a descriptor as a proc namespace file of mount type and takes a reference, else takes a reference on the current namespace; missing id and bad or wrong type descriptor yield distinct errors.

Request copy reads user size, rejects oversize and undersize, zero fills kernel storage then copies the variable length structure, enforces that by file mode forbids ids while by id mode forbids combining descriptor with id and requires mount id above the unique offset.

Query preparation validates the user range, clears state, stores mask and buffer descriptor, allocates scratch only when string class bits are requested, rejects a header only buffer in that case, and reports allocation failure distinctly.
Retry applies only to a specific transient overflow status, doubles scratch size with overflow and maximum read count guards; initial scratch accommodates three maximum length paths.

List preparation accepts cursor zero or above the unique offset, stores cursor and capacity, allocates the id array, takes a namespace reference and stores the parent filter; cleanup releases the root path, frees the array and drops the namespace reference.
Topology iterator returns the mount for the next or previous tree node according to direction flag, yielding null at tree ends.
Mount unique ids at or below the unique offset are invalid, except zero cursor meaning start of enumeration for list queries.
List state holds last seen unique id, parent filter id, kernel id array pointer, capacity, namespace pointer, and root path value.
Initial mount namespace is statically initialized with self initialized common field, initial user namespace, single passive reference, empty tree root, and initialized poll wait queue.
Namespace filesystem keeps a global mount pointer and a global root path value as static storage for its singleton instance.

Supported mask is the union of basic superblock, basic mount, propagate from, root, point, type, namespace id, options, subtype, source, option array, security option array, supported mask itself, uidmap and gidmap bits.
String class request set comprises root, point, type, options, subtype, source, option array, security option array, uidmap and gidmap; presence triggers scratch allocation.
Statmount accepts only the by file flag bit and listmount only the reverse flag bit; listmount rejects counts above one million to force iteration.

Single kernel unmount marks the mount short term then waits for read side grace before dropping the reference, ignoring error pointers; array form marks all first, uses expedited grace, then drops all references.

Mount membership test delegates to an internal mount check; chroot detection compares current root against the topmost overmount of the namespace root while holding mount reader protection, reporting mismatch or unmounted root.

Foreign root lookup and list enumeration require the namespace semaphore held for reading; both query entries acquire it in shared mode around the core operation, with list noted as needing protection only against topology changes.
Chroot check holds mount reader protection while resolving the topmost overmount; task namespace sampling holds the task lock; unmount paths rely on read copy update grace before final release.

Namespace install checks admin on target and chroot plus admin on caller user namespace, rejects anonymous namespaces and shared filesystem structures, swaps the namespace reference, looks up slash in the new namespace, rolls back on lookup failure else releases the old namespace and updates process home and root to the result.

Query lifecycle proceeds from request copy and namespace resolution through state preparation, guarded fill that may request larger scratch, user copy, then cleanup; transient overflow loops with larger scratch while other errors terminate.

Mount namespace type registers under short mount name with get, put, install and owner callbacks; get samples the task proxy under lock with a reference, put drops the reference, owner returns the owning user namespace.

Mount flags and idmap may change concurrently because only namespace read side is held; the code accepts possible skew between the two, relying only on single copy accessors to avoid torn reads without sequence retry.

Scratch overflow is signaled distinctly to trigger doubled retry, size addition overflow and user buffer exhaustion are terminal, and any failure copying payload or header to user aborts without partial success indication.

Filesystem namespace control table exposes mount maximum backed by a global unsigned integer with owner write and world read mode, integer vector min max handler and lower bound of one; init registers the table under fs during early boot.
